pr_body:
When dealing with index patterns, eg. `FROM logs-*`, some fields can have the same name but different types in different indices.

In this case we build an error message like 

```
Cannot use field [multi_typed] due to ambiguities being mapped as [2] incompatible types: 
[ip] in [test1, test2], [keyword] in [test3]"
```

With this PR, in case of many indices involved, we avoid listing them all, but we only list three of them and provide information about how many other indices are affected, eg.

```
Cannot use field [multi_typed] due to ambiguities being mapped as [2] incompatible types: 
[ip] in [test1, test2, test3] and [2] other indices, [keyword] in [test6]
```

(see the `and [2] other indices`)

Since these error messages are stored in `UnspportedAttributes` and serialized, this PR reduces significantly the size of a serialized execution plan with many type conflicts.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/111964

Related to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/111358
pr_title: ES|QL: shorten error messages for UnsupportedAttributes

review_comment: Since we're worried about very long lists of indexes, perhaps streaming and sorting these is not ideal? Removing the `sort()` should probably keep the stream shallow.
Although I realize this is harder to test, due to lack of deterministic ordering in sets.

I like the first three bit to be honest. The raw number of indices here isn't the problem so much as the length of the names times the raw number. But I think it's fine to sort them and grab the first three.
